category: open dataset API: NAS drive specifications and failure rates

free_tier.stated: No signup, no key, no rate limit: two read-only GET endpoints return the whole dataset of 298 drives, 21 with a measured failure rate, as JSON or CSV.
free_tier.notes: Both endpoints are cached for an hour. The failure-rate fields come from Backblaze Drive Stats.

per_object_cap.stated: no cap stated; the whole dataset is one 168410-byte JSON or one 28364-byte CSV

retention.stated: the live endpoints serve the current catalogue, cached for an hour; dated snapshots of the dataset are kept in a GitHub repository and in a Zenodo deposit

egress.terms: not applicable: a dataset API, not metered in bytes; both endpoints are cached for an hour

interface_detail: HTTPS GET of https://www.nasdisks.com/data/drives.json (a top-level object with license, count and a drives array) and https://www.nasdisks.com/data/drives.csv (the same rows, flat), open to all origins; an OpenAPI 3.0.3 contract at https://www.nasdisks.com/openapi.yaml also covers a third endpoint, /embed/cheapest.json
tooling: any HTTP client, such as curl with jq; the data page gives a Zenodo DOI to cite the dataset
chaining: Reference data on NAS and enterprise drives: specs, CMR/SMR recording technology and annualized failure rates derived from Backblaze Drive Stats, read as one JSON or CSV file. Bulk path: drives.json or drives.csv is the whole dataset in one GET, and dated snapshots of the dataset are in the GitHub repository deeddy/nas-drive-data and in a Zenodo deposit.

limits.value: none stated: the data page says no rate limit, and 40 parallel keyless GETs of drives.csv all answered HTTP 200

binding_note: No quota, key or rate limit is stated, and a 40-request parallel burst met no 429; the one-hour cache of both endpoints is the only limit on freshness.

identity_cost.detail: No signup and no key: the data page says so, and keyless GETs of both endpoints answered HTTP 200.

reliability_note: Both endpoints are cached for an hour, so an answer can lag the catalogue; both answered HTTP 200 to keyless GETs on 2026-11-02.
confidence_note: The data page states no signup, no key and no rate limit, and the repository README repeats no key and no rate limit; keyless GETs of drives.json and drives.csv answered 200 with the 298-drive count the page gives, and a 40-request parallel burst met no 429.
